headline: 15 injured as NCP leaders' convoy attacked in Habiganj
summary: Nasiruddin Patwary and Sarjis Alam were targeted in an attack by Chhatra Dal, leaving several injured and Sarjis Alam temporarily trapped.
details: A convoy carrying National Citizen's Platform (NCP) Chief Coordinator Nasiruddin Patwary and Chief Organizer Sarjis Alam was attacked by Chhatra Dal members in Habiganj on Tuesday evening.
The incident took place at the city's staff quarters, resulting in injuries to 15 people.
Following the attack, Nasiruddin Patwary sought refuge in the circuit house before departing for Dhaka.
Sarjis Alam was temporarily trapped inside a Sonali Bank branch, but was later rescued by police and brought to the circuit house.
Chhatra Dal has claimed that the tension arose due to provocative statements made by the NCP leaders.
The clash led to mutual chases and confrontations between members of the NCP and Chhatra Dal.
caption:

Following the attack, Nasiruddin Patwary sought refuge in the circuit house before departing for Dhaka.

Sarjis Alam was temporarily trapped inside a Sonali Bank branch, but was later rescued by police and brought to the circuit house.

Chhatra Dal has claimed that the tension arose due to provocative statements made by the NCP leaders.

headline_marked: 2 killed as [[college boundary wall collapses on TCB line]] in Mirpur
headline: 2 killed as college boundary wall collapses on TCB line in Mirpur
summary: A 45-year-old cleaner, who skipped lunch to buy subsidized rice, was among those killed when an 8ft-high wall fell on a crowd in Dhaka.
details: Two people were killed and at least six others injured when a boundary wall of Mirpur University College collapsed on a crowd waiting in a TCB queue in Dhaka's Mirpur-2.
The incident occurred around 1:27 pm on Love Road, where nearly 120 feet of the 8ft-high wall suddenly gave way, crushing people waiting for subsidized essentials from a TCB truck.

Among the victims was 45-year-old Nasima Begum, a cleaner who had skipped her lunch break to join the queue. She was declared dead at the National Institute of Traumatology & Orthopaedic Rehabilitation (Nitor).
Nasima earned Tk 13,000 a month and supported her mother and paid rent and debts, while her husband, a migrant worker in Kuwait, was unable to provide regularly.
Witnesses reported hearing a loud noise before the wall fell on the crowd, prompting bystanders to rush in and pull victims from the rubble.
A student of Mirpur University College noted that the wall had been built only a few years ago.
The Health Minister has announced that the government will bear the full cost of treatment for those injured in the collapse.
